misconceptions.believed: T2 W6's budgets could be sized by measuring the profiler against Python's standard library: 732 files in 12.5s is 17.1 ms per file, so 5,000 files would take about 85 seconds and exit criterion 6 would have to settle for a partial profile on an ordinary repository.
misconceptions.revealed_by: Building an actual 5,000-file repository and profiling it: 12.0s, 2.4 ms per file. The stdlib averages 16.6 KB per file against the synthetic repo's 1.3 KB.
misconceptions.corrected_to: Per-file cost and per-byte cost are different quantities and the stdlib is an outlier on the one I extrapolated through. A 5,000-file repository completes, so criterion 6 is met by finishing rather than degrading. The honest figure is 1.1-1.8 MB/s with analysis at 64% of the work, linear rather than quadratic.
misconceptions.generalisable_lesson: Extrapolating a per-item cost from a corpus whose items are twelve times the normal size sizes the budget for the wrong shape of input.

misconceptions.believed: The still-frame fallback for a stream that cannot animate was a property of the machine view, so the score reveal should inherit it.
misconceptions.revealed_by: Reading the piped transcript after wiring it in. Every piped play had gained twenty lines of box drawing, and therefore so had every CI log and captured transcript.
misconceptions.corrected_to: The fallback belongs to the command, not to the reveal. A still frame answers somebody asking to see the machine; the reveal is a live flourish with no business changing a non-interactive transcript. The reveal now draws nothing when the stream cannot animate, and the claim that piped output is unchanged is verified by diffing across the commit boundary rather than asserted.
misconceptions.generalisable_lesson: A fallback can be correct where it is written and wrong one caller up, which no test of the original module would catch.

decisions.decision: The machine is a vertical spine with loop return rails
decisions.rationale: Edge routing needs a graph layout engine: a dependency (N1) and a lot of code to draw diagonal lines. Sequence, loop, branch and return is what player solutions are made of.

decisions.decision: Frames come from the recorded trace, never from the source
decisions.rationale: A branch that never ran must never light up. Anything derived from the source alone is a diagram, not a run.

decisions.decision: render returns a Screen; frames are values
alternatives: Write to the terminal directly, as replay.py does
decisions.rationale: A frame that is a value is a frame a test can compare with no pty, and it keeps the module free of escape sequences.

decisions.decision: ui.Renderer.style added; vision emits no escape of its own
decisions.rationale: The rule is that ui owns escape sequences. editor.py rolling its own predates this and was left alone as out of scope.

decisions.decision: A compound statement owns its header line only
decisions.rationale: Owning the span puts the token in two boxes at once, which is a false claim about where control is rather than a drawing artifact.

decisions.decision: The reveal samples to 36 frames rather than shortening the delay
alternatives: Race all 400 frames inside the budget
decisions.rationale: Sampling keeps each frame legible and every counter true, because state is computed before sampling. 400 frames in 2.5s is a blur.

decisions.decision: A non-animating stream gets nothing in the reveal
decisions.rationale: The still frame answers a request to see the machine. Adding it to the reveal changes every CI log and piped transcript.
Nothing decorative may be able to break the reveal. A failed submission already has a failure block to read.

decisions.decision: The parked W6 VibeVector fields were reverted rather than left in place
alternatives: Keep them as groundwork for the next session
decisions.rationale: Three defaulted fields nothing sets is a persisted schema change with no behaviour behind it, and a later reader has to work out why partial is always false.

friction.description: Two rendering bugs shipped into the first draft and were caught by looking at output rather than by reasoning: the loop's return rail terminated on the loop's own body row so it never reached the code it returns from, and nested boxes kept a fixed width so right edges were ragged. Both now have tests, and both tests were confirmed to fail when the bug is reintroduced.

The --no-vision argument was inserted against a text anchor that matched earlier in the file than the p_play parser it belonged to, referencing an undefined name. Caught immediately by --help. Anchoring an edit on a string that appears more than once is the hazard.

The first scratch solution used >= where the level's reference uses >, so the run animated end to end was a 4/5 run rather than a clean pass. The animation was real; calling it a passing run would have been wrong.

handoff.state: The machine view ships in two places: vibecoder vision [run-id] on demand, and inside the score reveal bounded at 2.5s. 706 tests green unpinned, verify clean on 36 reference runs, showcase prints zero escapes in a pipe. Working tree clean.
handoff.next_action: T2 W6, started and parked. Two decisions were taken with the user and still stand: the vector records partial, partial_reason and files_seen, and a partial profile is saved and flagged. The field additions were reverted (D86), so W6 restarts from a clean models.py with those decisions already made - do not re-ask them. open_questions.question: The machine view has been judged by one person on one level. Does it read to somebody mid-solve, or is it decoration they skip? The --no-vision opt-out is the cheapest instrument available: if it gets used, that is the answer.
Sampling makes the step number jump, which is the cue that instants were skipped, but nothing says so. Is the jump enough, or should a sampled run be labelled as sampled?

_target_function picks solve, else the last function. A submission whose real work is in a helper draws the wrong machine and only says 'in helper()'. Should the view follow the call, or draw every function and let the token move between them?

This work belongs to no waypoint and is filed under a LANDED trajectory. Either T6 reopens, or the machine view and what follows it deserve a trajectory of their own. That is a call for the user rather than for a session looking for somewhere to file its entry.
